title: Constructing plasmid under GT DNA assembly standard
protocol: Design GTS oligos using the Oligo Designer for GT Standard Matlab App.
Install and run the Oligo Designer for GT Standard App.
Input name and sequence of the fragment (≥ 35 bp).
Click button “Click to design oligos for FRAGMENT” in the App interface.
Include converted G and T in the input sequence.
Design Foligos with or without phosphorothioate (PS)-bonds if the fragment length is longer than 90 bp.
Design Noligos (Non-modified fragment oligos) if the fragment length is less than 91 bp.
Dissolve GTS oligos in nuclease-free water to a final concentration of 100 µM.
Store dissolved GTS oligos at -20°C for long-term use.
Mix 1 μL of 100 μM Boligo, 2 μL of 10X T4 ligase buffer, 0.5 μL of T4 polynucleotide kinase, and 16.5 μL of nuclease-free water to prepare the phosphorylation reaction solution.
Incubate the reaction mixture at 37°C for 30 min.
Inactivate the T4 kinase by heating the reaction mixture to 65°C for 20 min.
Denature the DNA in the reaction mixture by heating it to 98°C for 2 min.
Anneal the Boligo by slowly cooling it from 98°C to 45°C at a rate of 0.1°C/s, then hold at 45°C for 2 min.
Further annealing by cooling the reaction mixture from 45°C to 4°C at a rate of 0.1°C/s and holding at 4°C.
Dilute 20 μL of phosphorylated and folded Boligo using 60 μL of nuclease-free water.
Store diluted Boligo at -20°C for long-term use.
Prepare PCR reaction solution by adding 1-5 μL template DNA, 0.3 μL G-Foligo, 0.3 μL A-Foligo, 25 μL Q5® Hot Start High-Fidelity 2X Master Mix, and ultrapure water to a total volume of 50 μL.

Perform PCR cycling: initial denaturation at 98 °C for 30 s; followed by 35 cycles of denaturation at 98 °C for 8 s, annealing at 55-65 °C for 15 s (based on primer melting temperature), extension at 72 °C for 20-30 s per kb; and a final extension at 72 °C for 2 min, then hold at 4 °C.
Mix PCR solution with 10 μL of 6X gel loading dye.
Load the mixture into two wells in a 1% agarose gel in Tris acetate-EDTA buffer.
Run gel electrophoresis at 150 V for 25-35 min.
Image the gel using Gel Doc EZ imager.
Cut two slices of gel containing appropriate bands and transfer them to 1.7 mL Eppendorf microcentrifuge tube.
Add 500 µL of binding buffer to the tube.
Dissolve the gel completely at 50 °C.
Load the solution onto the column.
Wash the column using 550 µL of wash buffer once.
Centrifuge the column at least at 10,000 g for 1 min.
Elute the solution using 40 µL of HPLC water (room temperature).
Mix 40 µL of purified DNA solution with 5.5 µL of 1 M Tris solution (pH 9) and 10 µL of 30 g/L iodine solution.
Incubate the mixture at 70 °C for 5 min in an Eppendorf ThermoMixer.
Dilute the treated solution with 250 µL of nuclease-free water and 350 µL of DNA extraction binding buffer.
Load the well-mixed solution onto the column.
Wash the column using 550 µL of wash buffer twice.
Dry the column by centrifuging at least at 10,000 g for 1 min.
Elute the solution using 30 µL of HPLC water (room temperature).
Store the prepared fragment at -20 °C for long-term use.
Anneal G-Noligo and A-Noligo in an annealing solution containing 50 µL of 100 µM G-Noligo and 50 µL of 100 µM A-Noligo.
Denature the annealing solution at 98 °C for 2 min.
Cool the denatured solution from 98 to 75 °C at a rate of 0.1 °C/s, hold at 75 °C for 2 min.
Cool further from 75 to 45 °C at a rate of 0.1 °C/s, hold at 45 °C for 2 min.
Anneal the solution from 45 °C to 4 °C at a rate of 0.1 °C/s and then hold at 4 °C.
Dilute the annealed fragments with nuclease-free water to a final concentration of 10-20 ng/µL.
Store the diluted fragments at -20°C for long-term use.

Mix 3 µl of prepared fragment (with 1-nt SEs) with barcoding reaction solution containing 0.3 μL of 1.25 μM LA-Boligo, 0.3 μL of 1.25 μM RG-Boligo, and 3.6 μL of Blunt/TA Ligase Master Mix to barcode a fragment.
Incubate the one-pot reaction mixture at 37 °C for 1 hour.
Incubate the one-pot reaction mixture at 25 °C for 10 minutes.
Hold the one-pot reaction mixture at 4 °C.

Prepare ligation PCR solution containing 1 μL of barcoding reaction solution, 0.3 μL of 100 μM RG-Aoligo, 0.3 μL of 100 μM LA-Aoligo, 25 μL of Q5® Hot Start High-Fidelity 2X Master Mix, and ultrapure water to a total volume of 50 µL.
Perform PCR cycling condition as per previous protocol step.
Isolate gel containing appropriate bands after gel electrophoresis.
Purify isolated gel containing appropriate bands.
Elute the column with 40 μL ultrapure water.
Mix 1 μL of plasmid solution with ultrapure water to achieve a concentration between 1 to 10 ng/μL.
Add 0.3 μL of 100 μM RG-Aoligo to the diluted plasmid solution.
Add 0.3 μL of 100 μM LA-Aoligo to the mixture containing the diluted plasmid and RG-Aoligo.
Mix 25 μL of Q5® Hot Start High-Fidelity 2X Master Mix with the previous components.
Top up the volume to 50 μL using ultrapure water for the PCR solution.
Prepare barcoded fragments directly from Step 5a 4 or 5b 2 if non-modified Aoligos are used.
Digest barcoded fragments prepared in Step 5a 4 or 5b 2 with restriction enzymes (REs) RE1 and RE2 if using the RE-based method.
Mix 1 μL of RE1, 1 μL of RE2, 1 μg of barcoded fragment, and 5 μL of 10X proper Buffer in a total volume of 50 μL with nuclease-free water for enzymatic treatment.
Follow general rules of restriction enzymes to avoid internal cutting sites.
Incubate the RE-digestion mixture at 37°C for 3 hours.
Separate the appropriate fragments using gel electrophoresis.
Purify the separated fragments using a column as described in Step 3a 4.
Obtain twenty-five microliters of enzymatically treated barcoded fragment from the previous step.
Perform an iodine-based cleavage reaction to treat barcoded fragments prepared in Step 5a 4 or 5b 2.
Generate long SEs at both ends of the barcoded fragment as described in Step 3a 5.
Obtain thirty microliters of purified barcoded fragment for subsequent assembling step using CLIVA method.
Determine the concentrations (ng/μL) of the barcoded fragments using NanoDrop or any similar device.
Combine 4 µL of 2X Gibson Assembly Master Mix and 4 µL of equimolar barcoded fragment mixture in the assembly reaction solution for up to six fragments.
Perform the assembly reaction at 50 °C for 15 min (for 2-3 fragments) or 60 min (for 4-6 fragments).
Use two microliter of the assembly mixture for transformation after the assembly reaction is completed.
Combine 1 µL of 5X In-Fusion HD Enzyme Premix and 4 µL of equimolar barcoded fragment mixture in the assembly reaction solution.
Perform the assembly reaction at 50 °C for 15 min.
Use one microliter of the assembly mixture for transformation after the assembly reaction is completed.
Combine 0.5 µL of T4 ligase, 0.5 µL of 10X T4 ligase buffer, and 4 µL of enzymatically digested barcoded fragment and backbone in the ligation solution (insert to backbone molar ratio of 3:1).
Perform the assembly reaction at 16 °C for 12 h.
Prepare an assembly reaction solution containing 1 μL of 10 mM MgCl₂ and 4 μL of equimolar barcoded fragments mixture (total 0.2-1 pmol).
Heat the assembly reaction solution in a thermocycler at 80 °C for 1 min, then decrease to 68 °C at default speed, keep for 10 min, and then decrease to 4 °C at 0.1 °C/s.
Mix 1 μL of assembly products with 17 μL of E. coli Dh5α heat-shock competent cells in a pre-chilled 1.7 mL Eppendorf microcentrifuge tube on ice for 5 min.
Heat-shock the tube at 42 °C in an Eppendorf ThermoMixer for exactly 35 s, then incubate on ice for 2 min.
Mix the cell solution with 150 μL of SOC medium and directly plate it on LB Agar plate containing proper antibiotic.
Incubate the plate at the temperature required by specific applications; colonies usually appear after 12-16 h when incubated at 37 °C.
Resuspend single colony in ultrapure water using 100 µL for colony PCR reaction.
Add 0.15 μl of forward oligo to the reaction solution.
Add 0.15 μl of reverse oligo to the reaction solution.
Mix 5 μl of Q5 High-Fidelity 2X Master Mix into the reaction solution.
Add 3.7 μl of nuclease-free water to the reaction mixture.
Incubate at 98 °C for 5 min for cell lysis and initial denaturation.
Incubate at 98 °C for 8 s for each cycle (denaturation).
Anneal at 55-65 °C for 15 s per cycle.
Extend at 72 °C for 20-30 s per kb for each cycle.
Repeat denaturation, annealing, and extension steps for 35 cycles.
Incubate at 72 °C for 2 min as a final extension.
Hold the solution at 4 °C after PCR cycling.
Mix 2 μl of 6X gel loading dye with the PCR solution.
Load mixed solution into one well in a 1% (w/v) agarose gel.
Run gel electrophoresis at 150 V for 25-35 min.
Image the gel using Gel Doc EZ imager.
Inoculate positive colony resuspension identified by gel electrophoresis into LB broth with proper antibiotic.
Culture cells overnight in a 50 mL falcon tube at required temperature.
Harvest cells from 10 mL of cell culture by centrifugation at 4,000 rpm for 10 min.
Extract plasmids from the obtained cells using a commercial plasmid extraction kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Obtain fifty microliters of plasmid solution (plasmid DNA is eluted from the column using elution buffer).
Send twenty microliters of the plasmid solution to a local sequencing service provider for sequencing verification.
Analyse the sequencing data received using Benchling or similar software.
Upload ab1 format data and align with plasmid sequence.
If mutation/insertion/deletion affecting the biological function is encountered, send out another plasmid for sequencing.

Ensure sequencing results cover important regions of the plasmid (e.g., barcode sequence with biological function [ribosomal binding site, 5’- and 3’-untranslated regions, protein linker, etc.] and coding sequence).
